Maintainer, 2026-09-30, deciding the review's gate and shape (D-WORKFLOW-102):

> "I think the council is right here. These reviews should happen in places and progressively over time. Also, I think it's good to examine different parts of the code base at different times, and it doesn't have to be a very broad sweep. We can also set up a separate milestone for this, and the first step for 0.0.2 may be performing the analysis of putting together the order of what we'd like to explore and how to do it. For example, we might want to start with security, or we may want to look at certain parts of the operating system that are the most brittle, or we may want to look at parts the closest related to new functionality in place, or we may want to look at functionality most related to changes we want to make, such as migrating away from the RetroArch UI and implementing our own."

This is the first item of `0.0.2` and the first child of #339 under the milestone "The adversarial review, in places". It produces the order and the method; it reviews nothing itself.

## What exists today

- #339 sizes the codebase in three tiers (the fork's own 121,000 lines; the 140,000 the image runs; the interface's 185,000) with packets of about 12,000 lines a seat, and the `code-auditor` skill at milestone tier with both council seats as the method used so far (the fix-round audits, `docs/audits/2026_09_2*`).
- D-WORKFLOW-102 sets the gate: `0.1` waits for the launch, control and state slice of Tier 1 and for any known serious finding; the interface's launch-path slice is reviewed before the fresh runner (#336 Step 1) replaces it.
- The four lenses the maintainer named: security; the most brittle parts of the operating system; the parts nearest new functionality already in place; the parts nearest planned changes, above all leaving the RetroArch interface.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `docs/reviews/order.md` exists and lists the slices in order, each with: the lens that put it there (security, brittleness, new functionality, planned change), the files or packages it covers with a line count from `tools/` or `wc -l`, the release it gates if any (per D-WORKFLOW-102), the method (the `code-auditor` tier and seats, or a lighter pass, with the reason), and the evidence that would close it (an audit folder, a punch list, a register row).
- [ ] The first three slices are sized to one audit each (packets under about 500 KB a seat, per `docs/audits/` precedent), and the launch, control and state slice of Tier 1 and the interface's launch-path slice are among them, since D-WORKFLOW-102 makes them gates.
- [ ] The order was itself put to the council seats as a preliminary review (the `review-formats.md` three-model format, advisory) or the reason it was not is recorded, and their material objections are answered in the document.
- [ ] Each slice has its own issue under #339 and this milestone, with the slice's files named, so `tools/box-check` can read them.
- [ ] `docs/decision-register.md` carries a row citing this issue for the chosen order, and #339's body links `docs/reviews/order.md`.


## Widened 2026-10-22: the plan for the plan comes first (D-WORKFLOW-181)

**Maintainer, 2026-10-22 (chat, D-QA-012):** *"To start, we'll need to assess the different areas of the codebase and develop a plan for how we'll move from section to section and best assess each part. The very first task will be developing a plan for our plan, so that we know how we can break this down into increasingly bite-sized chunks."*, *"The goal should be for us to develop a way of first surveying the entire codebase and understanding it, then breaking it down into a code review plan to go top to bottom across the entire codebase and work through it. I'd like to make sure that this plan is well defined so that it can be handed off in execution to an agent like Opus 5.5, as opposed to relying on Fable. I'd like to use Fable to develop all of the plan, the milestones, epics, issues, acceptance criteria, etc., and then be able to hand it off to a model like Opus 5.5."*, and *"We also do need to be cognizant of the fact that work will be happening in parallel, so there may be times where we need to go back and redo some of the review because new functionality may change the codebase. However, this should be a relatively small bit of work that needs to be redone compared to the sheer scope of the codebase."*

This issue is now **M6.P0**: the plan for the plan, `docs/reviews/plan-for-the-plan.md` on `feature/m6-renovation-plan-346` (worktree `/workspace/repos/pixelelated/distribution.worktrees/m6-renovation-plan-346`, from the fresh clone of D-INFRA-025). The order and the method (the criteria above) move to **M6.P1, the survey**, which the plan's § 6 specifies and which gets its own issue under #339; the criteria above stay here as the contract P1 must meet, and this issue closes when P0's criteria below are met and P1's issue carries them forward.

### Acceptance criteria for P0 (plan § 10)

- [ ] `docs/reviews/plan-for-the-plan.md` is on `next`, and `docs/reviews/README.md` names it, `order.md`, the inventory, the status table and the briefs directory with what writes each.
- [ ] `docs/decision-register.md` carries D-WORKFLOW-181 and D-INFRA-025 and `tools/register-check` passes on `next`.
- [x] Milestone 6 is named `M6: Codebase renovation`, its body opens with the current/next order of plan § 6; #339's title carries `M6:` and this issue's carries `M6.P0`; each body links the plan (read back from GitHub).
  Evidence, 2026-10-22: `gh api repos/pixelelated/distribution/milestones/6 --jq .title` → `M6: Codebase renovation`; its description's first line `## Current M6 plan — 2026-10-22T16:20:33Z`; `gh issue view 339/346 --json title` read back with the prefixes; `grep -c plan-for-the-plan.md` on both bodies ≥ 1.
- [x] The P1 issue exists under #339, titled `M6.P1 E339: The survey`, with plan § 6's six steps as its checklist, the three tools named (`tools/renovation-inventory`, `tools/renovation-drift`, `tools/renovation-status`), and the futro owed at its kickoff named.
  Evidence: #641, attached as a sub-issue of #339 (`gh api repos/pixelelated/distribution/issues/339/sub_issues` lists #346 and #641); its body carries the six steps, the three tools and the futro.
- [x] The P1 brief exists at `docs/reviews/briefs/p1-survey.md` with the ten sections of plan § 7, and a session with no context given only the repository and that brief reaches P1 step 1 without a question to the planner; its first ten commands are recorded on this issue (the D-WORKFLOW-133 proof).
  Evidence: two proofs, both read-only, both recorded in the comment of 2026-10-22 below. The first (version 1) stopped with sixteen questions; the second (version 2) reached the first inventory commit without a question, with two deviations it would have made on its own and one judgement call, all three folded into version 3 on `feature/m6-renovation-plan-346`.
- [x] `tools/forbidden-terms-check` exits 0 on the tree, `tools/work-log-index --check` passes, and `tools/ceremony-check` reports nothing newly owed by this lane, pasted here.
  Evidence, on the branch: `forbidden-terms-check: 0 hits in 133285 tracked files` (exit 0); `work-log index: current`; `register-check: 646 IDs, each once; every citation in the live documents names a row`; `tools/ceremony-check --gate` → `BLOCK weekly: 2026-W42 summary missing` and `box-check: ... 1 fail` (#637), both the M7 lane's, its W42 summary present on its unmerged branch; `tools/box-check --issue` 339/346/640/641 → `0 fail` each.

### Open questions (plan § 11)

The milestone's name; the executor model and effort; depth defaults (settled 2026-10-22: the § 6c defaults stand, D-WORKFLOW-184, the RELAYED comment below); where the EmulationStation survey runs; **one canonical session stash with two lanes writing it** (this lane keeps its state in `.github/sessions/saved-session-state-feature-m6-renovation-plan-346.md` and does not edit `saved-session-state-next.md` while M7 owns it); when the legacy checkout retires (#640).

Can this be done on the VM? No test is proposed by P0; every behaviour claim a slice makes is proven on the VM under the plan's evidence floor.

## Continuing execution across lanes — 2026-11-02

Maintainer request (verbatim):

> let's ensure that our codebase renovation plan is continuing to work across all lanes according to the work we've defined in in the Milestone. It looks like we might have idle lanes.

Observed: all five worker lanes had completed their last bounded work and were idle. The immediate dependencies are coordinator-owned: T39 remediation brief, T41 Stage-B acceptance, and T42 proved brief/dispatch. Existing work and accepted stages are preserved.

- [ ] The M6 body and current coordinator handoff name every wN worker's assigned work or concrete dependency, owner and next action; Herdr readback confirms actual activity for each dispatch.
- [ ] T39 receives its proved stream brief incorporating D-WORKFLOW-223/-224 and #1407; its lane acknowledges the exact branch, scope and completion boundary.
- [ ] T41's Stage-B artifacts are reconciled against the live criteria and D-WORKFLOW-222; the resulting acceptance or concrete correction is posted on #688 and delivered to T3.
- [ ] T42's brief is proved and corrected, its live criteria/ownership and area futro updated, and its named worktree/branch explicitly dispatched to T5.

Can this be done on the VM? No — this coordination proof reads the tracker, immutable artifacts and Herdr states. Source-only checks use small local scratch; no runtime allocation, physical or cloud action is introduced.
